claim: A marketing blog asserts that reaching 100 subscribers puts a channel ahead of 63% of all YouTube channels and that the average time to reach 1,000 subscribers is around 22 months, but the first figure links to a vidIQ page that now returns HTTP 404 and the second carries no citation at all.
stance_target: The provenance of commonly circulated YouTube growth and time-to-monetization figures
scope_conditions: BerryViral, a thumbnail-optimization SaaS marketing its own product; article undated and unbylined; every numeric claim is sourced to another SEO page or a free-tool benchmark rather than to primary data; a direct fetch of the cited vidIQ URL on 27 July 2026 returned a 404 error page
quoted_support: The average timeline to hit 1,000 subs is somewhere around 22 months. Reaching just 100 subscribers puts you ahead of 63% of all YouTube channels.
numbers: cited vidIQ source URL returns HTTP 404

claim: The article's own time-to-1,000-subscribers benchmarks are internally inconsistent, giving 6-12 months in one section and roughly 22 months as the average in another, with no sample size, year or country attached to either.
stance_target: Any use of vendor blog benchmarks as evidence on time from starting to first meaningful income
scope_conditions: Same page, two adjacent sections; neither figure states a sample size, year, country or methodology
quoted_support: At this stage, reaching 1,000 subs typically takes 6-12 months of consistent effort (3-4 videos per week). For hobbyists or ultra-niche channels, that timeline stretches to 1-2 years.
